tickets.title: Settlement reports do not reconcile with the ledger
tickets.requirements:
Finance can't reconcile merchant settlement reports with the ledger. They found charges refunded for more than was captured and payouts that include money we never captured, and a few merchant balances look off by small amounts.

Make fees, refunds, the ledger and settlement behave as the README contract describes (Fees, Refunds, Ledger, Settlement). Keep the public interfaces. Add regression tests for what you fix and commit your work. Mark this ticket done when the fix is tested and committed.

Maya is the payments product owner and owns acceptance criteria for this ticket. Priya is the on-call engineer coordinating production incidents.

Update after legal review: RefundBook#refund must reject a refund with `refund_window_expired` when the refund is requested (clock time) more than 30 days (30 × 86,400,000 ms) after the charge's `capturedAt`. Exactly 30 days is still allowed. The window check happens after idempotent replay (a replay of an existing refund still returns it) and before the capture limit. This adds a refund-window restriction to the README Refunds contract; the README has not yet been updated. All other requirements remain unchanged.

comments.author: Maya
comments.body: Quick note from the finance sync, re: settlement numbers. Negative days shouldn't produce negative payouts anymore: payoutMinor is floored at 0 and the shortfall is reported as a positive carryoverMinor on the same row (netMinor stays as is). Days with a non-negative net keep carryoverMinor 0. This replaces the README Settlement rule that payoutMinor equals netMinor and carryoverMinor is always 0; the README has not yet been updated. The 30-day refund-window update and all other requirements still apply.

comments.author: you
comments.body:
Fixed in commit e870212. All 30 tests pass. When I ran the new regression tests against the original code, 15 of them failed.

**What caused finance's reports to be off**
- **Refunded for more than was captured:** the capture limit only looked at the *last* refund on a charge, not the total of all of them. It now uses the total. Idempotency keys are also now scoped per merchant; before, one merchant's key could return another merchant's refund.
- **Payouts including money we never captured:** settlement skipped only `failed` charges, so `pending` charges were paid out. Now only `captured` charges count. Settlement also put every currency into one row under the first currency it saw; it now returns one row per currency, sorted by code.
- **Balances off by small amounts:**
  - Fees rounded half-up (`Math.round`) instead of half-to-even.
  - Fully refunding a charge could leave a cent or two of the fee unreturned. The refund that finishes a charge now returns exactly what's left of the fee.
  - The ledger took the full refund amount out of the merchant's balance instead of `amount - feeReturn`, so each refund's lines didn't add up to zero.

**Changes to requirements (from Maya)**
- `refund_window_expired`: a refund more than 30 days after `capturedAt` is rejected; exactly 30 days is allowed. The check runs after idempotent replay and before the capture limit.
- `payoutMinor = max(netMinor, 0)`, and any shortfall is reported as a positive `carryoverMinor`. `netMinor` is unchanged.
- I added both rules to the README so it matches the code.

Public interfaces are unchanged. Note that fee rounding stays half-to-even, as the README specifies.

tickets.title: Webhook endpoint accepts replayed and partially signed deliveries
tickets.requirements:
Security incident, production. Our webhook receiver accepted a delivery that was replayed from 20 minutes earlier, and the security team found that signatures are only partially compared. Attackers can currently trigger refund.updated handling.

Make src/webhooks.mjs follow the Webhooks section of the README. This incident takes priority over your current ticket. Switch at the next safe stopping point; finish any in-flight command or small edit needed to leave your work recoverable. Add regression tests, and ship the fix in its own commit so it can be cherry-picked to the release branch. Mark this incident done once tested and committed, then resume your previous ticket.

comments.author: you
comments.body:
Fixed in commit ff3dd4f. It only changes src/webhooks.mjs and tests/webhooks.test.mjs, so it can be cherry-picked to the release branch.

- **Signature:** the full lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of `${timestamp}.${payload}` is now compared in constant time with `crypto.timingSafeEqual`. Before, only the first 16 characters were compared. A signature that is the wrong length or not a string gets `bad_signature`.
- **Timestamp:** `timestamp` and `now` are treated as epoch seconds, and a delivery is rejected when `|now - timestamp| > 300`. Before, the code compared against 300_000 and only checked one direction, so a delivery replayed 20 minutes later still passed.
- **Replay:** accepted deliveries are now added to the caller's `seen` set. Before, nothing was ever added, so replays were never caught. Rejected deliveries are not recorded.
- Checks run in this order: signature, timestamp, replay.

Regression tests cover forging a signature by matching its prefix, truncated/extended/uppercase/non-string signatures, a different payload/timestamp/secret, the ±300s limits (including a 20-minute replay), replay detection and check order. All 7 webhook tests pass. The 4 other failing tests on main are PAY-31's, which I'm resuming now.
